correctness.rationale: For n=0 or 1 the natural partition works. For n=2, if the merge surplus is nonpositive the singleton partition works; if positive each player's Shapley gain over the singleton is exactly half that surplus. For n=3, independent exact subset-weight calculations (python3 /workspace/checks/check124.py, record 1) gave singleton payoffs (2,2,0), pair payoffs (5/2,5/2), (1,-1), (1,-1), and grand payoffs (19/6,19/6,-1/3). Both fair partitions have a strict gain of 1 from a merge; the other three are unfair. The split phase does nothing at {12,3} and the unique legal merge takes it to {123}, strictly lowering the vector from (0,5) to (-1/3,6). At {123} the residual {12} is fair, so the next composite returns to {123}; in separate split and merge steps this is a two-cycle. No tie or update-order assumption is needed here. Zhu–Han's primary §§3.1–3.3 use this operator and Lemma 3 asserts the disputed conclusion under nonnegative singleton values. Theorem 2 conditions on monotonicity separately and is not refuted. Coalition values here are all nonnegative but not monotone.
